interface.title: Computational Life Lab
interface.field: Artificial life / origin-of-life simulation (BFF primordial-soup self-replicator emergence)
interface.stage_of_work: Running simulation experiments and doing exploratory analysis of them (live monitoring, single-organism inspection, replicator detection, comparing runs)
interface.what_it_is_for: Run a BFF primordial-soup simulation of random 64-byte programs epoch by epoch and examine it: population grid and diversity/entropy/complexity metrics, per-organism genome, lineage and instruction distribution, a hand-stepped interpreter debugger for a pair of tapes, replicator scans, checkpoint/resume through a run browser, and metric overlays across stored runs.

data.note: No files were uploaded. Every population is generated by the built-in engine from the bundled YAML configs (bff_dev.yaml, bff_baseline.yaml, bff_population_sweep.yaml) and a seed. A Run #1 (seed 12345, epoch 0) already existed at load. I made Run #2 (seed 42, stepped to epoch 70, checkpoint at 60) and Run #3 (seed 7, epoch 20, checkpoint at 20). All are stored in runs/dashboard_runs.db. Stepping is slow, about 3 s per epoch at population 512.

tree.general: Simulate a population of self-modifying programs with no imposed selection, and study whether and how self-replicating structure emerges
tree.specific: Run BFF primordial-soup experiments from any bundled soup config (bff_dev, bff_baseline, bff_population_sweep) and analyse populations, organisms, pairwise executions, replicator candidates and stored runs
